answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement, so the closest prior success is regional failover (memory_b2), which restored latency without dropping the path. Rollback is unavailable because the in-flight security patch must stay. Circuit breaking would fail writes we are required to keep. Read-replica routing addresses dashboard/read load, not this write path. Adding capacity is a weaker fit once the surge is already on and the fault is regional rather than global; verifying b3 only to confirm that. In-flight settlement writes make failover non-zero dual-write/loss risk, and RCA is still unconfirmed (timing also lines up with the release), so uncertainty is retained while shifting traffic off the degraded region.
